Server-side rendering vs client-side rendering for SEO

Server-side rendering is safer for search indexing than client-side rendering, because a crawler sees the content in the first byte of HTML rather than after script execution. Verified 2026-08-14.

The trade is engineering cost: server-side rendering moves work to first response and needs a runtime, while client-side rendering ships a shell and fills it in the browser.

When client-side rendering fails

It fails when the crawler does not execute JavaScript, when the primary content is injected after a network call, or when the rendered HTML differs from what a user sees.
